blocks.html:
“Happy to meet — send me a time.” Three emails later you’re still trading calendar screenshots, and the client has gone quiet.

Or worse: a client books a 30-minute call, no Teams link ever arrives, and they sit looking at an empty window while you’re on another call. Or a booking lands on top of a meeting that was never in your Zoho calendar, because nothing checked it.

All three are the same problem: your availability lives in one place and your bookings happen in another. Zoho Bookings fixes that in about 20 minutes of setup — and then every future client does the calendar work for you.

By the end of this lesson you’ll be able to:

  1. Verify your personal booking page presents you professionally — photo, bio and URL.
  2. Connect Outlook and Microsoft Teams so bookings check your real calendar and arrive with a working meeting link.
  3. Control your availability, breaks and buffers so the page protects your time.
  4. Test your live link the way a client would, and fix what they’d see.

About 20 minutes. You’ll need your Outlook calendar open too.

The difference the page makes

Scheduling by emailScheduling with your booking page
Four emails to agree a time; the client picks something you can’t do.They see only the times you’re genuinely free, and book one.
No meeting link until you remember to send it.Teams link generated automatically, every time.
Back-to-back calls with no room to write notes.The 15-minute buffer is already built in.
Your availability is whatever your inbox says it is.Hours, breaks and conflicts come from one place you control.

The rest of this lesson is the five settings behind that page.

1. Your consultant profile

This is the first thing a client sees. Treat it like the front page of a proposal.

  • Sign in to Zoho Bookings and open Consultants in the left menu.
  • Open your own profile — you’ll see tabs for Profile, Availability, Assigned Consultations and Integrations.
  • Photo: professional headshot.
  • Bio: one or two sentences on your expertise. It builds trust before they click a slot.
  • URL: should read bookings.oneaccord.co/.

blocks.label: In Zoho Bookings
blocks.instructions: Open Zoho Bookings → Consultants → your profile. Check your photo, bio and booking URL, and update anything that’s missing or out of date.
blocks.confirmText: My consultant profile is up to date — continue

blocks.html:
2. Outlook and Teams: where double-bookings come from

Without these two connections the page is only guessing at your diary.

  • Calendar: Integrations tab → Office 365 / Outlook Calendar → Configure → sign in. Turn Check for Conflicts on for your primary work calendar.
  • Video: in the Video Conferencing section, authorize Microsoft Teams. Every booking then generates its own link.
  • Other calendars: link any second calendar you keep commitments in — this is also where you confirm everything is actually syncing.

Conflict checking is only as good as what you connect. A meeting that lives in a calendar you didn’t link is invisible, and the page will happily book over it.

blocks.label: In Zoho Bookings
blocks.instructions: Open your profile’s Integrations tab. Confirm three things: Office 365 / Outlook Calendar connected with Check for Conflicts on, Microsoft Teams authorized under Video Conferencing, and any other calendar you keep commitments in linked as well.

blocks.html:
3. Availability: your hours, your breaks

  • Availability tab → Customize working hours for this staff.
  • Set start and end times for each day. Not the same every day? Set them separately.
  • Add breaks — a lunch hour, a school run, a no-meeting block for writing. Breaks are how the page protects thinking time, not just meetings.
  • Check your time zone. A wrong time zone is the most common reason a client says “I booked 2 p.m. and nobody came.”

blocks.label: In Zoho Bookings
blocks.instructions: Open the Availability tab. Set your hours day by day, add any breaks you actually take, and confirm your time zone. If you work across time zones with clients, note how the page presents your hours to someone in a different zone.
blocks.confirmText: My availability and time zone are set — continue

blocks.html:
4. Services and the 15-minute buffer

  • You’re assigned two standard templates: the 30-minute and the 60-minute appointment. Those are the two OneAccord offers by default. Other durations exist in the system for exceptions but aren’t meant to be on your page day to day.
  • Both include a 15-minute buffer after the appointment for notes and preparation. You don’t set it — the system protects the time for you.
  • Check that both templates are active on your services list. If one is missing, ask the admin rather than building a replacement.

blocks.label: In Zoho Bookings
blocks.instructions: Open your services list and confirm the 30-minute and 60-minute appointment templates are both active. If one is missing, note it and raise it with the admin before moving on.
blocks.confirmText: Both service templates are active — continue

blocks.prompt: A client books a 30-minute call and confirms by email — but no Teams link arrives. Where do you look first?
options: The Video Conferencing integration in your Bookings profile
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes — if Microsoft Teams isn’t authorized under Video Conferencing, the booking is created without a link. Fixing the integration fixes every future booking too.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Start with the Video Conferencing integration: if Microsoft Teams isn’t authorized, bookings are created without a link. The buffer and Outlook settings don’t generate meeting links.

blocks.promptHtml:
A colleague sends you their booking link to test, because clients have been complaining. Three things are wrong:

  1. Clients can book over meetings that are already in the colleague’s Outlook calendar.
  2. Bookings arrive without a Teams link.
  3. Two clients this week turned up an hour early.

Diagnose each one: what setting is behind it, and what would you change? Then say how you’d check the page from the client’s side once it’s fixed.
rubric: Traces the double-booking to calendar integration and Check for Conflicts (or to an unlinked second calendar)
Traces the missing Teams link to the Video Conferencing integration not being authorized
Traces the hour-early arrivals to a wrong time zone in the profile or availability settings
Tests the fix from the client’s side — opening the booking link in a private window and stepping through a real booking
blocks.coachContext: Lesson on Zoho Bookings setup. Correct mapping: (1) bookings over existing meetings = Outlook/Office 365 integration not connected or Check for Conflicts off, or a second calendar not linked; (2) no Teams link = Microsoft Teams not authorized under Video Conferencing; (3) clients arriving at the wrong hour = incorrect time zone on the profile or availability. Verification: open the booking URL in an incognito/private window, check photo, both service durations, availability matching Outlook free time, buffer applied, Teams link generated. Booking URL format bookings.oneaccord.co/<name>. Standard services 30 and 60 minutes with a 15-minute buffer set by the system. Admin handles missing service templates.

blocks.promptHtml:
Now the harder, more common case. Three requests arrive in one week:

  1. A prospect wants a 45-minute introductory call — “all our vendors do 45.”
  2. A client in another time zone says the only slot that works for them is outside your published hours.
  3. A long-standing client asks you to book a Saturday morning directly, rather than through your page.

For each: what do you do, and what do you change (if anything) in your Zoho setup?
rubric: Handles the 45-minute request without quietly creating a new service — either offers the 30 or 60 minute template or routes the exception for approval
For the time-zone request, checks what the client actually sees and offers a real slot rather than changing published hours permanently
For the Saturday request, books it without pretending the page handles it — and keeps the record of the meeting consistent
Keeps the buffer and calendar accurate so the exception doesn’t create a double-booking
blocks.coachContext: Transfer case: exceptions to a standardised booking setup. Standard services are 30 and 60 minutes with a 15-minute buffer; other durations exist for exceptions but should not be offered day to day, so an unusual duration is either mapped to a standard template or raised for approval rather than created ad hoc. Availability changes are deliberate, not reactive; one-off meetings outside published hours can be booked manually as long as the calendar stays accurate and the buffer is respected. Consistency between the booking page and the real calendar is the whole point. OneAccord values: truth, compassion and service — say what's actually possible.

blocks.label: Apply it in Zoho Bookings
blocks.instructions:
Run the client-side audit on your own page.
  1. Copy your individual booking URL (bookings.oneaccord.co/).
  2. Open it in a private/incognito window so you see what a client sees.
  3. Run the checklist: photo visible, bio reads well, both 30 and 60-minute options offered, availability matches your Outlook free time, time zone right, Teams link appears on a test booking.
  4. Add the link to your Outlook email signature, and open Share to look at the QR code — useful when you meet someone in person.
  5. Cancel any test booking you created, so it doesn’t sit on your calendar.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve audited my booking page as a client and fixed what I found — continue
